defectsFound.summary: A caller chose the identity their rate limit was counted against.
defectsFound.mechanism: clientIp took the leftmost x-forwarded-for entry, which the client writes. A rotating header bought eight public intake submissions against a cap of three, each creating a lead and queueing research.
defectsFound.fix: TRUST_PROXY_HOPS declares how many proxies may be believed, default 0. With N hops the trustworthy address is the Nth from the right, so prepended entries cannot move it.

defectsFound.summary: The mutation war's own verdicts came from the exit status and were wrong in two opposite directions.
defectsFound.mechanism: A suite that skipped for want of a runtime exited 0 and was reported as a surviving guard -- loud but false. A mutant that broke a module at import time exited non-zero and was reported as KILLED -- silent, and it inflated the count that every other guard is judged by.
defectsFound.fix: Verdicts are read from what each run reports. SUITE_DID_NOT_RUN and NO_ASSERTIONS_RAN are named separately from real survivors. Four suites that announced an absent database with a passing test now use a real skip, which is why the deterministic run reports 51 skipped rather than 48.

defectsFound.summary: Two defects found by writing the mutations for the above.
defectsFound.mechanism: A mutation anchor appearing both in the code and in the registry entry quoting it mutated the registry instead, ran an unmutated tree, and reported the guard as surviving. Checking every anchor then found SCAN-01 matching two sites, so one branch had never been attacked -- and it turned out to be unreachable.
defectsFound.fix: applyMutation refuses an ambiguous anchor; the verdict logic moved to its own module so the registry no longer contains the code it points at; the unreachable branch was removed and the concern it aimed at is now proven rather than assumed.

defectsFound.summary: A subscription that had not paid booked cleared revenue.
defectsFound.mechanism: subscription_created fires for every subscription state including a free trial. The one-time branch of the classifier has always checked whether the order was paid; the subscription branch did not. Measured: on_trial, past_due, unpaid, cancelled, expired and paused each booked $99 and marked the lead paid -- $594 nobody paid, reconciling as PROVIDER_CLEARED_PAYMENT_PROVEN on every surface.
defectsFound.note: Every surface agreed because all three triple-witness views derive from the same signed webhook. Consistency across three views of one event cannot catch a misreading of that event.
defectsFound.fix: An allowlist of statuses that mean money moved, applied to subscription_created only. subscription_payment_success is untouched because a recovery payment legitimately arrives with a past_due status.

defectsFound.summary: The money did not have to cover the product it unlocked, and a free order booked list price.
defectsFound.mechanism: The product is a query parameter on the checkout link the buyer holds. Measured: $49 bought the $299 review, $0.01 bought monitoring, $0.00 bought strategy. The zero case also revealed `detail.amountCents || listPrice` treating a genuine 0 as absent, so a free order booked $299 of cleared revenue.
defectsFound.fix: An underpayment in the pricing currency is REVIEW_REQUIRED -- the only classification an operator is shown -- rather than a refusal, because a discount code is a real reason to pay less.

The public report/artifact/checkout surface: tokens leak nothing on any guess, traversal or wildcard; artifact ids refuse traversal; checkout issues nothing without a valid token.
Webhook signature admission: nine forgery shapes all refused with 401, none creating money.

isStaleSignal compares a signal's age against a maxAgeMs the caller supplies, so a caller can already choose its own answer without discarding anything. Protecting its callers would look like a boundary and enforce nothing. A test asserts they stay editable, with that reason, so nobody tidies them in later.
